hook.line: Tomás has opened the café at six every morning for months. Don Hernando has noticed, and for a man who says very little, he finds the words.
hook.en: I'm very proud of you. (a man speaking, to a friend)

examples.en: I'm very proud of you. (a woman speaking, to a friend)

examples.es: Don Hernando está orgulloso de Tomás.
examples.en: Don Hernando is proud of Tomás.
I'm proud to be Colombian. (a man speaking)
We're proud of our neighbourhood. (all men, or a mixed group)

examples.es: Estamos orgullosos de que trabajes aquí.
examples.en: We're proud that you work here. (to a friend)
I'm not proud of that. (a woman speaking)

rule:
English says proud *of* someone. Spanish keeps the same little word, *de*, in every version:
*orgulloso de* + a person or thing: *de ti*, *de mi familia*.
*orgulloso de* + an action you did yourself: *de ser colombiano*.
*orgulloso de que* + someone else's action, with the wish form you met with feelings: *de que trabajes aquí*.
*Orgulloso* is an adjective: *orgullosa*, *orgullosos*. After *de*, you is *ti* and me is *mí*.
Use *estar* for pride in someone. *Ser orgulloso* means being a proud, stuck-up person.
smallPrint: Teachers call the verb form after *de que* the subjunctive: it appears when you react to what someone else does.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *con* and type the whole sentence: *Estoy muy orgullosa ___ ti.*
yourTurn.why: Proud of someone is *orgulloso de*, as in English.

yourTurn.prompt: Say to a friend (a man speaking): I'm proud of you.
yourTurn.why: After *de*, you (informal) is *ti*, with no accent.

yourTurn.prompt: Say (a man speaking): I'm proud to live in Bogotá.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy orgulloso de vivir en Bogotá.
yourTurn.why: An action you do yourself is *de* plus the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Don Hernando is proud of Tomás.
yourTurn.answer: Don Hernando está orgulloso de Tomás.
yourTurn.why: A feeling right now uses *está*, and *de* comes before the person.

yourTurn.prompt: Say (we are all women): We're very proud of our neighbourhood.
yourTurn.answer: Estamos muy orgullosas de nuestro barrio.
yourTurn.why: We are all women, so the adjective is plural feminine: *orgullosas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about a woman speaking: *Estoy orgulloso de mi familia.*
yourTurn.why: The ending follows who feels the pride: *-a* for a woman.

yourTurn.prompt: Start with *Estoy orgulloso de que…* (a man speaking) and say: I'm proud that Tomás is staying.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy orgulloso de que Tomás se quede.
yourTurn.why: Someone else's action after *de que* takes the wish form: *se quede*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Soy orgulloso* describes a proud, stuck-up person; for pride in someone, use *estoy*.

pitfalls.right: Estoy orgulloso de que trabajes aquí.
pitfalls.why: The *de* stays in front of *que*, just as it stays in front of *ti*.
The adjective matches the person who feels proud, and *ella* is a woman.

personal: Say one thing you are proud of doing, with *estoy orgulloso de* (or *orgullosa de*) plus an infinitive. Then name one person you are proud of.
